STEP 1 — goal: read the five frozen bundles and decide what actually separates the proposals, since every candidate is in scope and no ablation arm is run.
READ: workspace holds only progress.jsonl; the bundles are in the task text. Per-bundle anchors compared across all five: E5 train-graph statistic (118,315 edges / 115,582 distinct over 24,556 items, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, edge_density 5.3266); E6 baseline SID diagnostic (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted_null 0.067); E11 PASS geometry_operator_valid; E12 **FAIL** behavior_dependency ("a positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged (measured: True), so it can never move an assignment; a codeword-dependent weight moved … top-1 indices"); E13 PASS geometry_dependency ("the matched Euclidean intervention changed 1 of the top-1 indices"); E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN in every bundle; experiment ledger E18–E25.
OBSERVED: (a) all five keep Sinkhorn and take the hard index as row-argmax of the balanced plan (criterion 6 satisfied, none out of scope); (b) all five inject a codeword-dependent, not row-scalar, behaviour offset (m_k via sigmoid, s_k=sigmoid(a_k) quantiles, a_k=tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||), rhat_k centred radius, b_k from a first Sinkhorn plan), so none is trivially inert per E12 — but E12 sets the bar: a per-code offset must be large enough to reorder top-1, and E13 shows the curved-vs-Euclidean difference itself moves only 1 of 6 indices, so a small normalised offset will not act; (c) E5 shows a sparse graph (mean out-degree 5.45), so triangle-closure t_ij is near-zero for most pairs and every triangle-based rho/kappa/s_i is weak and popularity-adjacent — this penalises mechanisms that apply the offset broadly or add an unnormalised second loss, and rewards level-1-only, scale-relative, single-offset designs; (d) E6 shows the baseline L1 prefix already sits 0.0907 vs 0.067 null, so the coarse level is exactly where the small behaviour signal lives; (e) ledger E18–E25: best recorded Stage3 test R@10 is 0.0546 (BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL), then 0.0544 (CURV-RESID-CONTRAST), 0.0517 (CONCMID-GEO-SID), 0.0500 (COOC_RANK_FRECHET), 0.0482 (BEHDIR-L4), 0.0446 and 0.0306 (BRad-RQ); all comparable_to_frozen=false, none near 0.065.
REASONING so far: with no ablation and one run, the discriminators are mechanism hygiene under the binding policy (derived constants, level-1-only intervention, bounded single offset inside the unchanged balanced assignment) plus survival of E12/E13 magnitude limits. curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1 is cleanest on exactly these: only the level-1 cost matrix changes, no extra loss, beta = m/R_c frozen from a measured step-0 median, D = ceil(mean degree) data-derived, c = 1 the framework default, a_k init at the equiprobable quantiles of a uniform rank marginal so balance turns the offset into an equiprobable curvature partition — the only design whose structural claim is checkable by Spearman(rho, s_k1). cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1 has the tightest single gradient loop (L_curv on the same plan trains the same m_k that sit in the cost, c measured from init embedding scale, all denominators variance-normalised) but spreads the behaviour offset to all three levels while its motivation is the coarse prefix, and fixes a Gaussian bandwidth s=0.25 with a 1.0 multiplier. CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN is close behind (lambda_b and lambda_curv scale-derived by stop-gradient, behaviour offset level-1 only, geometry at all levels) but carries a second alignmen

t loss that flattens toward a bimodal encoding (its own risk list) and a per-batch median lambda_b. hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 normalises d_c by D_med yet sets lambda=1 on a [-1,1]x(-1,1) product so the offset is commensurate with the whole distance term, uses an unnormalised homophily weight lambda=1 beside reconstruction, and leaves rhat_k sign arbitrary (E12/E13 say that is where it breaks). scc-l1-curvcoherence is last: two Sinkhorn passes plus detached running b_k buffers, a hard-coded 0.25 offset weight in the spec that its own risk line describes as a derived half-median cap (constant provenance defect under policy), and a W=5 window that departs from the baseline graph; its own risk list names inertness.
OPEN: turn this into the 1..5 ranking and the objection line. Next record carries the final answer.

STEP 2 — FINAL ANSWER (complete). Ranking of all five proposals, best first, each grounded in the frozen bundle evidence; all five were checked against the scope contract and all five keep the baseline balanced Sinkhorn with the hard index taken as row-argmax of the plan (criterion 6 satisfied), so the placement turns on E5 (sparse train graph: 118,315 edges / 115,582 distinct over 24,556 items, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526), E6 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted_null 0.067), E11/E13 (valid operator but only 1 of 6 top-1 indices moved by the Euclidean swap), E12 FAIL (row-scalar behaviour weights are inert; only codeword-dependent offsets can move assignments), E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN (no joint path exercised for any candidate) and the ledger E18–E25 (best recorded Stage3 test R@10 = 0.0546 BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL, then 0.0544 CURV-RESID-CONTRAST, 0.0517 CONCMID-GEO-SID, 0.0500 COOC_RANK_FRECHET, 0.0482 BEHDIR-L4, none near the 0.065 target, all comparable_to_frozen=false).

because E13 shows the curved-vs-Euclidean change moves only 1 of 6 top-1 indices and E5's graph is sparse (mean out-degree 5.45), a single bounded offset confined to the level E6 shows carries the behaviour signal (0.0907 same-prefix vs 0.067 null) is the lowest-risk way to make the coupling real."}, {"idea_id": "cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1", "position": 2, "reason": "Tightest single gradient loop of the five and so the best answer to E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN: the per-code curvature centre sigmoid(mu_k) sits in the Sinkhorn cost AND is trained by L_curv on that same balanced plan, with beta_l = 1.0*median_i min_k d_c measured no-grad at init, rho rank-uniformised (median 0.5, MAD 0.25) and every denominator variance-normalised, and c measured from the init embedding scale rather than fixed; placed second only because E8 spreads the behaviour offset to all three levels while its own motivation and E6's prefix statistic concern the coarse level, and its Gaussian bandwidth s=0.25 with a 1.0 multiplier are chosen, not derived, constants."}, {"idea_id": "CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN", "position": 3, "reason": "Policy-compliant on constants (lambda_b = rho_b*median d_c/(median|s_i|*median a_k) and lambda_curv stop-grad-matched to 10 percent of L_recon, no history, no sweep), behaviour offset at level 1 only where E6 locates the prefix signal, and a_k=tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||) is genuinely codeword-dependent so E12's inertness trap is avoided; below the top two because it adds a second curvature-covariance alignment loss whose own risk list concedes a possible bimodal curvature split, and its per-batch median lambda_b is noisy - extra failure surface on E5's weak triangle signal with no ablation arm to isolate it."}, {"idea_id": "hyperbolic_behavio

E12 (row scalars inert, per-code offsets must actually reorder top-1) and E13 (Euclidean swap moves only 1 of 6) put the risk squarely on that unnormalised magnitude, and delta_ij is a hand-designed homophily target rather than a measured quantity."}, {"idea_id": "scc-l1-curvcoherence", "position": 5, "reason": "Ranked last on specification and verifiability, not on idea: it needs two Sinkhorn passes plus detached running m_k/s_k buffers so the realised plan is driven by a stale curvature target, its spec states a hard-coded 0.25 offset weight while its own risk line describes that cap as derived from half the batch median curved distance (a constant-provenance defect under the binding no-sweep policy), and it builds the graph with a W=5 window rather than the baseline's; its own risk list names the inertness failure mode ('numerically close to behaviour-off'), and with E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN in every bundle this is the heaviest joint path of the five to verify in a single run."}], "objection": "All five bundles share the same evidentiary hole, and it caps how much any placement can be grounded: E14 is CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN for every candidate (no proposal's own quantizer path has been exercised, so the joint behaviour-geometry dependency is asserted, not shown), E12 is FAIL for the shared proxy (a positive row scalar can never move an arg-min, and only a codeword-dependent weight moved top-1 indices), and E13 shows the matched Euclidean intervention moves just 1 of 6 top-1 indices, so any normalised offset must be large enough to reorder top-1 or the mechanism is inert by construction. Compounding this, E5 describes a sparse train graph (118,315 edges, 115,582 distinct, 118315/24556 items, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526), where triangle-closure t_ij is near-zero for most pairs, so every triangle-based rho_i/kappa_i/s_i in these five proposals is weak and popularity-adjacent; E6 shows the baseline level-1 prefix already holds only 0.0907 same-prefix rate against a 0.067 permuted null; and the only observed Stage3 evidence (E18-E25) tops out at 0.0546 (BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL), then 0.0544 (CURV-RESID-CONTRAST), 0.0517, 0.0500, 0.0482 - all flagged comparable_to_frozen=false and none within 0.01 of the 0.065 target. The ranking therefore rests on mechanism hygiene under the one-run, no-ablation, no-sweep policy (level-1-only intervention where the behaviour signal demonstrably lives, a single bounded codeword-dependent offset inside the unchanged balanced assignment, and derived rather than chosen constants), not on any measured behavioural signal or demonstrated headroom; a single frozen run at the top-ranked candidate cannot by itself separate a real coupling effect from the seed noise that the policy deliberately leaves inside the interval."}
